transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I was sent by occupational health. I’ve gotten into a pattern of putting off breakfast and lunch when I’m busy with lab runs or exhibition work, and then when I do eat, it’s something very small and controlled.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
Yes. If the number on the scale goes up even a little, I get this sharp panic—like I’m losing the discipline I’ve worked so hard to keep.
Are you currently underweight for your height?
I think so. My clothes are definitely looser, and the number has kept going down. Part of me sees that as proof I’m staying focused, though, not letting work chaos spill over into my body.
Does your body weight have a big effect on how you feel about yourself as a person?

Yes. Before I go to the lab, I look in the mirror and I don’t really see myself as thin. I focus on my stomach or my hips, and if they seem noticeable, I feel careless—like I don’t look serious or disciplined enough.
Are you doing things on purpose to keep yourself from gaining weight?

Yes. I’ve gotten into a pattern of pushing breakfast and lunch aside when I’m doing lab runs or exhibition work. Then when I finally do eat, I keep it very small and controlled. Occupational health sent me because of that.
